analysis.title: Market Monitor, Week Ending October 23, 2026
key_insights: US equities were little changed on the week (S&P 500 -0.46%). An early-week tech rebound was followed by a sharp sell-off on concerns about the sustainability of AI investment and ongoing geopolitical risks.

The US 10-Year Treasury yield fell 19bp on Thursday, its biggest daily drop since March 2023. Weak tech and turmoil in France drove safe-haven buying. The 2-Year and 10-Year ended the week at 4.68% and 4.99%.
French 10-year bond yields hit their highest level since 2002 on fiscal deficit and political instability concerns, tied to continued protests and unrest. The Bund 10-year yield fell to 3.34%.

Brent rose to $116.72/bbl while WTI ended near flat at $103.27/bbl as the Middle East conflict escalated. Tankers near the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy facilities came under attack, and there were reports of strikes on Iran. WTI is described as less exposed to Middle Eastern supply shocks.
Gold fell sharply to $3,996.10/oz as rising oil prices boosted expectations of rate hikes.

The dollar index softened 0.03% after Fed Chair Warsh suggested there was little urgency to tighten policy further. That raised expectations that the Fed holds at its meeting next week. The dollar strengthened against the euro ($1.1202) and weakened against the yen (¥156.87).

Chart of the Week: the AI trade has driven much of this year's gains and pushed market breadth near record lows. The median S&P 500 stock stayed roughly 15% below its own peak even as the index hit all-time highs. Non-AI stocks have rallied sharply as the AI theme came under pressure, which GSAM sees as an early sign that leadership may be broadening.

About 80% of early-reporting S&P 500 companies beat 3Q earnings estimates, but market reactions to beats have been muted. Attention has shifted from headline beats to margin durability, earnings quality and the viability of guidance through 2027, as investors weigh higher yields.
Large banks reported strong results: NII guidance expanded into 2027 as fixed-rate assets reprice, equities trading surged and credit metrics stayed benign. Bank stocks still reacted poorly.

GSAM believes the market is trading financials on the idea that higher rates mean selling financials, with attention on unrealized losses on bond portfolios that pressure capital. Most banks giving guidance expect interest income and net interest margins to keep rising into 2027. GSAM views the capital pressure as largely a timing issue, with regulatory changes potentially supporting buybacks in 2027.

Several bank CEOs flagged a once-in-a-generation capital shortage to finance the AI boom. They rejected third-party agentic AI transacting on client accounts because of security concerns, while internal AI tools scaled rapidly.
The top 10 US banks captured roughly 85% of Q3 deposit growth, and one bank alone captured 30%.

GSAM's credit team sees AI credit demand as intact but funding now separating winners from the rest. It stays cautious and prefers secured, amortizing loans against collateral and contracts over unsecured bonds.
US consumer: financial companies report resilient consumer activity and generally healthy credit trends. A GSAM consumer analyst notes pressure at lower income tiers but no broad deterioration.

US S&P Global Composite PMI fell to 57.6 in October from 58.4, still near a five-year high. Eurozone composite PMI fell to 51.9 from 53.1, more than expected, partly because of French protests. UK composite PMI rose to 53.1 from 52.0, an eight-month high.
UK CPI rose to 3.5% YoY in September from 3.1%, above the 3.4% consensus, driven by motor fuel prices. Core CPI rose to 2.8% from 2.6%, reinforcing expectations of a BoE hike at its next meeting.
US initial jobless claims fell 6k to 194k for the week ending October 17, below the 200k consensus and at levels not seen since the 1960s.
Week ahead: the Fed decision on October 28 is expected to hold at 4.0%, the ECB and BOJ decide on October 29, and Euro Area Q3 GDP is due October 30.

sector_views.rationale: GSAM sees an opportunity in the gap between bank fundamentals (rising interest income and margins into 2027) and share reactions focused on rate-driven capital pressure, which it views as a timing issue.
Non-AI stocks have rallied as AI comes under pressure. GSAM sees early signs of broadening leadership and stresses the value of diversification.

risk_factors: Sustainability of AI investment spending and AI-related funding strain, including a capital shortage flagged by bank CEOs.
Middle East escalation lifting oil and rate-hike expectations.
French fiscal and political instability spreading to European bond markets.
Higher yields pressuring margins, earnings quality and bank capital through unrealized bond losses.
Muted market reaction to earnings beats and the viability of guidance through 2027.

vol_and_positioning: The VIX fell 2.70% on the week but is up 19.03% month to date and quarter to date.
Market breadth is near record lows because of AI concentration. The median S&P 500 stock is roughly 15% below its own peak.
geopolitical: The Middle East conflict continued to escalate, with tankers near the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy facilities under attack and reports of strikes on Iran.
Continued unrest and protests in France pushed French bond yields to their highest since 2002 on fiscal deficit and political instability concerns.

tension_points.bull_case: Banks guide to rising interest income and net interest margins into 2027, with strong equities trading and benign credit. Capital pressure is a timing issue and regulatory changes could support 2027 buybacks.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher rates create unrealized losses on bond portfolios that pressure capital, and the market is trading financials on the idea that higher rates mean selling financials.

theme_stances.key_argument: As the AI theme comes under pressure, non-AI stocks have rallied sharply, which may signal broader market leadership.
The market is trading on higher rates meaning selling financials, while bank interest income and margins are guided higher into 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: The potential opportunity lies in the gap between those effects.
